title: Ireland's Budget Billions Fail to Quell Household Anxiety · 12 Oct
keywords: Ireland, Budget 2027, cost of living, inflation, public sector pay, strikes, Fiscal Advisory Council, corporation tax, ECB, household energy costs, trade unions, Irish economy, public services, fiscal policy, European affairs
notes: Ireland's government has unveiled an €8.5 billion budget package designed to ease the cost-of-living burden on households, but inflation is forecast to remain above the European Central Bank's 2% target through 2027, and public-sector unions are preparing nationwide strikes that could cancel up to 150,000 medical appointments. The twin pressures of persistent price rises and threatened disruption to essential services are testing whether the country's considerable fiscal firepower is translating into meaningful security for ordinary citizens. At the heart of the debate lies a more fundamental question about the durability of Ireland's spending model.
